title: Prospect Wireframe: Competitive Signal Heatmap & Intervention Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a reproducible, lightweight prototype (wireframe) that synthesizes multi-source competitive signals into a time-aware heatmap and defines a set of automated intervention protocols for product and sourcing owners. Background: We have many model-supply and feature signals (benchmarks, availability events, pricing shifts, quantization cadence) scattered across trackers. This ticket consolidates a minimal product definition + research plan to validate whether a combined heatmap + rule-driven intervention can reduce alert noise and surface high-confidence risks for Dedicated/Private customers. Scope: - Ingest prioritized signals (latency regressions, price spikes, deprecations, new variant releases) for top 8 model families. - Produce a weekly heatmap view with time decay and confidence scoring. - Define 4 intervention templates (monitor, notify, throttle-route, fallback-model) with trigger thresholds. - Deliver a one-click playbook for SEs and PMs to run a simulated incident and evaluate remediation efficacy.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap prototype deployed to internal dashboard with sample data for 8 model families
Signal pipeline documented and reproducible (ingestion steps + schemata)
Four intervention templates implemented as annotated runbook entries
Pilot run completed with two product teams and feedback captured
deliverables: Confluence PRD: 'Prospect Wireframe - Competitive Signal Heatmap'
Internal dashboard tile (Grafana/Metabase) with heatmap and drilldowns
Signal ingestion scripts in repository (scripts/heatmap-ingest) and README
Intervention playbook PDF and checklist for SEs/PMs
approach: Phase 1: Discovery (this ticket) — assemble signals, define scoring, interview SE and two PM stakeholders. Phase 2: Wireframe — lightweight ETL + heatmap + static runbook for interventions. Phase 3: Pilot — run simulation against historical events and collect SLO/alert metrics. Use iterative 1-week sprints for feedback loops.
success_metrics: Reduction in false-positive competitive alerts by >=30% during pilot
Time-to-detect high-impact model-availability events reduced by >=25%
Clear mapping from signal to intervention in >=80% of pilot cases
